**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse both targets from each guide identity**

For Norman identities such as `SET_KLF1__SET_KLF1`, `rsplit("_", 1)[0]` returns only `SET`, so a genuine two-gene perturbation is reported as a single; conversely, `NegCtrl0_BAK1__NegCtrl0_BAK1` becomes `NegCtrl0` and is reported as a control. This corrupts the committed class counts, perturbation counts, fold assignments, and downstream dataset audit; parse all non-control target tokens from the construct identity instead.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare donor leakage against a donor-held-out split**

The `frozen` and `donorleak` calls use the identical group-based train/test rows, with every donor represented on both sides; the only change is whether the estimator consumes donor means. Thus `dl_p - frozen_p` measures the benefit of a donor feature, not inflation relative to the preregistered donor-clean holdout, and E3 can pass without the evaluator ever detecting a donor split leak. Add an actual donor-held-out comparison before reporting this negative control as passed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Complete independent verification before finishing the round**

This record marks the round `ROUND_FINISHED`, but neither its artifact list nor the accompanying round report records an independent Verifier/Skeptic check; a repository-wide search finds only the requirement itself. Closing the round without that check bypasses the mandated research workflow, especially significant here because the committed metadata audit and leakage control contain result-affecting errors.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare donor regimes on identical test rows**

Here `dl_p` is computed over all held-group cells from all four donors, while `dc_p` is computed after `donor_holdout=True` filters the test set to donor 3 only. Subtracting correlations from different test populations confounds donor leakage with test composition; on donor-3 rows alone, both predictors are constant and both Pearson values are zero. Build the leaky and clean training regimes around the same multi-donor test rows before using this gap to pass E3.

Nevertheless, the evaluator labels E1, E3, and E4 `pre_registered_checks`, and this report claims all four were preregistered. Mark those checks as post-hoc or evaluate them in a newly admitted round with their thresholds frozen in advance.

When the donor diagnostic runs, fresh evidence in `fe2924c` is that both calls omit `donor_holdout=True`, so the exclusion branch at lines 173–183 never executes. Consequently, `donorclean` trains on every test donor and merely disables the donor-mean feature, meaning the reported 0.1869 gap remains feature benefit rather than donor-split leakage despite the JSON and report claiming test donors were unseen; construct clean and leaky training sets with different donor exposure while retaining identical test rows.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use identical targets for the primary leakage gap**

For the preregistered E2 comparison, `frozen` tests every cell in groups 6–7, whereas `leaky` tests selected genes from every group (the committed result confirms 1,496 versus 770 test cells). Since the synthetic group effects differ, subtracting these Pearson values confounds leakage with target-cohort difficulty; the donor diagnostic now enforces same-T, but the primary verdict does not. Select one held-gene test set and vary only whether its functional siblings enter training before using the gap to declare `LEAKAGE_DEMO_PASS`.

The current implementation deliberately gives CLEAN only non-T-donor training rows while LEAKY retains all non-held rows, and the committed result/verifier measure a 0.1616 gap; this remediation summary instead says the training rows are identical and reports 0.1869. In the exact follow-up commit this is fresh contradictory evidence about both the method and metric, so update the report to describe the donor-exposure difference and the reproduced 0.1616 result.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove functional siblings from the CLEAN training set**

Both `run_same_T` calls build the identical training set containing every non-held gene, so CLEAN still has all functional-sibling rows; `siblings=False` merely ignores the computed group means and substitutes a constant predictor. Consequently the reported 0.8776 gap measures a group-aware estimator versus a global-mean estimator, not inflation caused by sibling exposure under different splits, and cannot support `LEAKAGE_DEMO_PASS`. Filter sibling rows from CLEAN training while retaining the same test rows, or describe this as a model ablation rather than leakage.
